title: Add explicit supplier payment-to-invoice allocations
description: Link the existing canonical supplier-payment evidence to ERP-065 supplier purchase-invoice evidence through explicit, auditable allocation rows. Reuse existing payment records rather than creating another payment master. Do not initiate a payment, infer links, post accounts payable, alter bank or tax data, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation audits and reuses the existing canonical supplier-payment evidence and ERP-065 supplier invoice records, leaving one payment master, one invoice register and one explicit allocation model.
Authorized users can allocate an eligible active supplier-payment evidence record to one or more recorded supplier invoices using persisted identifiers only.

The server requires authoritative Supplier and currency compatibility, rejects unavailable or voided records, duplicate payment and invoice pairs, non-positive values and allocations above either the payment's available amount or the invoice's unallocated gross amount.
Partial allocation and one-to-many or many-to-one allocation are supported while unallocated payment and invoice amounts remain separately visible and are never silently written off.
Different currencies are never combined or converted unless an authoritative persisted conversion already belongs to the source evidence; no current or guessed exchange rate is used.
Allocation rows preserve payment, invoice and Supplier snapshots, allocated amount, recorder and recorded time; client-supplied snapshots, balances and audit fields are not trusted.
An incorrect allocation can be voided with a bounded reason while preserving its original values and history; hard deletion, reassignment and silent amount replacement are not provided.
Purchase Order allocations, invoice allocations and payment-to-invoice allocations remain distinct evidence dimensions and are not added together as if they represented separate payments.
Missing allocations are displayed as none or unknown and are not interpreted as unpaid, paid, settled, overdue, tax-deductible or posted status.
Creating, reading or voiding an allocation does not change payment evidence, invoice status, Purchase Orders, receipts, Supplier balances, inventory, tax, bank, finance or settlement records.
Queries and summaries are bounded and avoid per-row access; schema changes are idempotent and validated only through permitted local or test-database paths.

Unit and integration tests cover partial and full allocation, multiple invoices and payments, Supplier and currency mismatch, duplicate and over-allocation rejection, void history, unavailable records, bounded summaries and source-record non-mutation; safe validation passes and browser acceptance is recorded as deferred during development.

scenarios: Allocate one existing supplier-payment evidence record partially across two compatible recorded supplier invoices and verify payment and invoice unallocated amounts without changing any source record or initiating a payment.
Attempt duplicate, excessive, Supplier-mismatched and currency-mismatched allocations, verify rejection, then void a valid allocation and confirm its original values and reason remain in history.

human_gate.reason: Explicit allocation of existing repository evidence only. Real payments, bank access, accounting posting, production database mutation, deployment and release remain behind mandatory human gates.
